| Shift with the arrows   | a list with `multiple`    | Select the run of items to the one you reach                 |
| Ctrl+A (Command+A on a Mac) | a list with `multiple` | Select every item that can move, or none                    |
| Escape                  | a list with a selection   | Let go of the selection                                      |
| Up, Down, Home, End     | a sortable tree           | Move between the rows that show. The tree is one tab stop    |
| Right                   | a branch                  | Open it, or go to its first item if it's open                |
| Left                    | a row                     | Close a branch that's open, or go to the row's branch        |
| Enter                   | a row                     | Open or close a branch; `onAction` on anything else          |
| Space                   | a row                     | Pick it up with everything under it, or drop it              |
| Up, Down                | a row that's picked up    | Move it between the rows that show                           |
| Left, Right             | a row that's picked up    | Take it out a level, or in one                               |
| Escape                  | a row that's picked up    | Put it back where it was                                     |

With a pointer: drag an item. With `multiple`, press an item's check, or Shift-click,
Command-click or Control-click it, to select; dragging a selected item carries the selection.
In a tree, drag a row up or down, and sideways a level for every 20px; a press on a branch
opens or closes it. In right-to-left text, Left and Right swap.

## For agents

- **SortableList** is listed by its `label`, with each item as data (`{ value, label,
  position }`). `moveItem(item, position)` moves an item, by its key or its label, to a
  place counted from 1; pass a list of items to move several, in their order.
  `selectItems(items)` sets the selection, with `multiple`. Moving a locked item, or a name
  the list doesn't have, fails and says why.
- **SortableTree** is listed by its `label`, with each item's level and branch.
  `moveItem(item, into, position)` moves an item and what's under it into a branch (`null`
  for the top level), at a place from 1 (the end without one). `expandItem` and
  `collapseItem` open and close branches, and `openItem` runs `onAction`. A move into an
  item that isn't a branch, into itself, or of a locked item fails and says why.

## Web Components

`<uiset-sortable-list>` and `<uiset-sortable-tree>` are in
[Web Components](./web-components.md#content-and-forms), on the same primitives:

```html
<uiset-sortable-list id="playlist" label="Playlist" multiple></uiset-sortable-list>
```

```ts
const playlist = document.querySelector("uiset-sortable-list")! // typed by @uiset/web
playlist.items = [
  { value: "intro", label: "Intro", description: "0:48", locked: true },
  { value: "harbor", label: "Harbor Lights", description: "3:52" },
]
playlist.addEventListener("valuechange", (e) => save(e.detail.value)) // preventDefault() refuses
```

- `items` is a property. `value` (the order) and `selected` are live: reading gives a copy,
  and setting them fires nothing. Keys a set order leaves out follow it, in `items`' order.
- `label`, `multiple`, `numbered`, `orientation` and `help` are attributes.
- It fires `valuechange` and `selectedchange`, and `api` has `moveItem` and `selectItems`.

```html
<uiset-sortable-tree id="pages" label="Pages" icons></uiset-sortable-tree>
```

```ts
const pages = document.querySelector("uiset-sortable-tree")!
pages.items = [{ value: "guides", label: "Guides", children: [] }, { value: "faq", label: "FAQ" }]
pages.expanded = ["guides"]
pages.addEventListener("itemschange", (e) => save(e.detail.value)) // the items, nested again
```

- `items` and `expanded` are live: after a move, `items` reads the tree as it is. Setting
  them fires nothing.
- `label`, `icons`, `max-depth` and `help` are attributes.
- It fires `itemschange`, `expandedchange` and `action`, and `api` has `moveItem`,
  `expandItem`, `collapseItem` and `openItem`.


<!-- docs/rich-text.md -->

# Rich text

A rich text editor on UI SDK: headings, lists (nested, numbered, to-dos), quotes, code,
links, mentions, dividers and images, with a toolbar, Markdown as you type, "/" for blocks
and "@" for people. Its value is a small document you can save as Markdown or clean HTML,
and agents read and write it as Markdown through UI SDK's bridge.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @uiset/rich-text
```

It has no editor library underneath. The toolbar is UI SDK's Toolbar, Toggles, Select and
Popover; "/" and "@" are UI SDK's TriggerMenu, connected through an editor adapter; undo
is UI SDK's `createUndoStack`. The editing itself (`rich-text/view.ts`, `model.ts`) is
shared by React and Web Components.

## Parts

| Part               | What it is                                                                 |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RichTextEditor`   | The editor: toolbar, text, "/" and "@" menus, an optional count, a form value |
| `RichTextContent`  | Saved text, read-only, in the editor's styles (rendered as React, never as an HTML string) |
| `toMarkdown`, `fromMarkdown`, `toHTML`, `fromHTML`, `toText` | The document to and from Markdown, HTML and plain text |
| `richTextCommands` | What "/" offers by default, to extend or reorder                           |

## Use

```tsx
const [doc, setDoc] = useState(() => fromMarkdown(saved))

<RichTextEditor
  label="Release notes"
  value={doc}
  onValueChange={setDoc}
  placeholder="Write the release notes…"
  mentions={[{ value: "ada", label: "Ada Lovelace" }]}
  maxLength={2000}
/>

// Later: save it.
await save({ markdown: toMarkdown(doc), html: toHTML(doc) })
```

- `defaultValue` takes Markdown or a document, for an editor you don't control. `value`
  takes a document; pass back what `onValueChange` gives you (it fires for edits, not for
  caret moves).
- In a form, `name="notes"` adds a hidden field with the HTML (or Markdown, with
  `format="markdown"`).
- `maxLength` shows a count. Going over is allowed and says so in words ("12 over the limit
  of 2000 characters"), so nothing typed is lost; the field is described by the count.
- `commands` replaces what "/" offers: `{ value, label, description?, icon? | glyph?,
  run(state) }`, where `run` returns the next editor state (`setBlock`, `insertBlock` and
  the rest of `rich-text/model` are there for it). `commands={[]}` turns "/" off.
- `uploadImage(file)` takes pasted, dropped and chosen images; return `{ src, alt? }` or
  `null`. Without it, the toolbar has no image button and image files aren't taken.
- `readOnly` hides the toolbar and refuses edits from people and agents; `disabled` also
  dims it.
- `messages` changes what's announced (marks and blocks turning on and off), for other
  languages.
- `onSubmit` runs on Mod+Enter outside a to-do, for a comment box that sends.

## Safety

Everything that comes in is checked the same way typing is: pasted HTML and Markdown, the
editor's own clipboard format (any page can put it on the clipboard), a `value` or
`defaultValue` document, and what `RichTextContent` shows. Unknown block types become
paragraphs, heading levels and list depths are clamped, and links and images that aren't
`http(s)`, `mailto:`, `tel:` or a path (not `//host`) are dropped, also when a link is
added at a caret with nothing selected. `sanitizeDoc` from `rich-text/model` does it for
your own code.

## The document

A flat list of blocks, each `{ id, type, content }`: `paragraph`, `heading` (`level` 1–3),
`quote`, `code` (`language`), `bullet`, `ordered`, `task` (`checked`) with `indent` 0–4,
`divider` and `image` (`src`, `alt`). `content` is text runs with `marks` (`bold`,
`italic`, `underline`, `strike`, `code`, `link`) and mentions (`{ type: "mention", id,
label }`). It's plain JSON: store it as is, or store Markdown or HTML and read it back.

- **Markdown out** is GitHub-flavored: `- [ ]` tasks, fenced code, `~~strike~~`, nested
  lists by two spaces. Underline has no Markdown; it's kept in HTML only.
- **HTML out** is a small, fixed set of tags (`p`, `h1`–`h3`, `ul`/`ol`/`li`, `blockquote`,
  `pre`/`code`, `strong`, `em`, `u`, `s`, `a`, `hr`, `img`, `br`), with tasks as
  `<li data-checked>`. Text is escaped; links are `http(s)`, `mailto:`, `tel:` or a path.
- **Mentions** are `<span data-mention="id">@Name</span>` in HTML and read back as
  mentions; Markdown has no mention syntax, so there they're plain `@Name` text. Store the
  document or HTML to keep them.
- **HTML in** (paste, `fromHTML`) keeps only what the editor can show. A table's rows
  become lines with their cells apart by tabs. Images in pasted pages come in only when
  you pass `uploadImage` (no hotlinks or tracking pixels otherwise). Scripts, styles,
  event attributes, `javascript:` links and unsafe images are dropped. Bold, italics and
  strikethrough set by Google Docs' and Word's inline styles are read as marks.

## Keys

| Keys                       | Does                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Mod+B, Mod+I, Mod+U        | Bold, italic, underline (on the selection, or for what you type next) |
| Mod+Shift+X, Mod+E         | Strikethrough, inline code                            |
| Mod+K                      | Add, edit or remove the link at the selection         |
| Mod+Alt+0, 1, 2, 3         | Text, Heading 1, 2, 3                                 |
| Mod+Shift+7, 8, 9          | Numbered, bulleted, to-do list                        |
| Tab, Shift+Tab             | In a list: nest the item one level deeper, or less    |
| Enter                      | New block; on an empty item, out one level, then out of the list; twice at the end of a code block, out of the code |
| Shift+Enter                | A line break in the same block                        |
| Mod+Enter                  | Check a to-do off, or `onSubmit` elsewhere             |
| Mod+Z, Mod+Shift+Z         | Undo, redo (typing is grouped; an agent's edit is one step) |
| "/" at the start of a line | The block menu: arrows, Enter or Tab, Escape          |
| "@"                        | Mention someone from `mentions`                       |

Markdown as you type: `#`, `##`, `###`, `-`, `1.`, `[ ]`, `[x]`, `>` and a space at the
start of a line; `---` or three backticks then Enter; `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``
and `~~strike~~` as you close them. Pasting Markdown text turns it into blocks.

A to-do's box is a checkbox named by its task; a click or a screen reader's activation
checks it off. Each block takes its own text direction (`dir="auto"`), so Arabic or Hebrew
reads right in a left-to-right app. A read-only editor stays in the Tab order so its text
can be read and copied. Text from an input method takes the marks typing would there.

The toolbar is one Tab stop; arrows move along it. Pressing a button keeps the selection
and puts focus back in the text. Marks and blocks turning on and off are announced.

## For agents

The editor is one component, named by its `label`, with its value as Markdown.
`setValue(markdown)` replaces the text (unchanged Markdown changes nothing),
`insert(markdown)` adds blocks at the end without re-reading what's there, so mentions and
line breaks inside items survive, and `clear()` empties it. Each is one undo step for the person, and read-only or disabled
editors refuse them with a reason. The toolbar is hidden from agents (it acts on a
person's selection); agents format through Markdown instead.

## Web Components

`<uiset-rich-text>` is the same editor, built from UI SDK's own elements. See
[Web Components](./web-components.md#rich-text).


<!-- docs/chat.md -->

# Chat

A chat interface on UI SDK, in five items: the thread and its messages, Markdown answers
that stream, the parts around an answer (reasoning, tool calls, sources), the message box,
and the list of chats. Every part takes plain props, so your model's stream goes into your
own state and the kit draws it. The `chat-app` template puts them together into a page.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @uiset/chat @uiset/chat-response \
  @uiset/chat-parts @uiset/chat-composer @uiset/chat-sidebar
```

Each of the last four brings `chat` with it. `chat-response` also adds `react-markdown`,
`remark-gfm`, `remend` and `shiki`.

The behavior is UI SDK's. The thread is a `ScrollArea` that follows new text with
`stickToEnd`, and its controller brings you back from Jump to latest; the message box brings back what you sent with `createInputHistory`; "/" and "@" are
`TriggerMenu`; attachments are `FileInput`; reasoning, tool calls and sources are
`Collapsible`; the model picker is a `Select`; usage is a `Meter`.

## Parts

| Part                                  | Item            | What it is                                                     |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ChatThread`                          | `chat`          | The scrolling log: follows new text unless you scroll up, then offers Jump to latest |
| `ChatMessage`                         | `chat`          | One message: who sent it, when, its content and an `actions` slot |
| `ChatMessageActions`                  | `chat`          | Copy, Retry, Edit and Good or Bad under a message, as one toolbar |
| `ChatBranch`                          | `chat`          | "2 of 3" with Previous and Next version, for regenerated answers |
| `ChatEmpty`, `ChatSuggestions`        | `chat`          | The empty thread's heading, and prompts to start from          |
| `ChatTasks`                           | `chat`          | A plan: each task's status in words, and "1 of 3 done"         |
| `ChatShimmer`                         | `chat`          | "Thinking…" with a shimmer                                     |
| `ChatResponse`                        | `chat-response` | The model's Markdown, completed while it streams; raw HTML never renders |
| `ChatCodeBlock`                       | `chat-response` | Highlighted code with Wrap and Copy (`ChatResponse` uses it for fenced code) |
| `ChatReasoning`                       | `chat-parts`    | The model's thinking: open while it streams, then "Thought for 4s" |
| `ChatTool`                            | `chat-parts`    | A tool call: its status in words, input, output or error       |
| `ChatSources`, `ChatCitation`         | `chat-parts`    | "Used 2 sources", and a numbered link with a hover card        |
| `ChatImage`                           | `chat-parts`    | An image with its size reserved and an optional caption        |
| `ChatComposer`                        | `chat-composer` | The message box: Enter sends, commands, mentions, attachments, a toolbar |
| `ChatModelPicker`, `ChatUsage`        | `chat-composer` | A model `Select`, and a meter that reads "18.4K of 200K tokens" |
| `ChatThreadList`                      | `chat-sidebar`  | The chats: choose one, New chat, Rename, Delete (asks first)   |
| `ChatLauncher`                        | `chat-sidebar`  | A floating button that opens the assistant in a panel          |

## Use

```tsx
<ChatThread label="Conversation">
  {turns.length === 0 && (
    <ChatEmpty title="What are we working on?">
      <ChatSuggestions suggestions={["Draft release notes"]} onSelect={send} />
    </ChatEmpty>
  )}
  {turns.map((turn) =>
    turn.from === "user" ? (
      <ChatMessage key={turn.id} from="user">{turn.text}</ChatMessage>
    ) : (
      <ChatMessage
        key={turn.id}
        from="assistant"
        avatar={{ fallback: "AI" }}
        streaming={turn.streaming}
        actions={!turn.streaming && (
          <ChatMessageActions text={turn.text} onRetry={() => retry(turn.id)}
            feedback={turn.feedback} onFeedbackChange={(f) => rate(turn.id, f)} />
        )}
      >
        {turn.reasoning && (
          <ChatReasoning streaming={turn.thinking} seconds={turn.seconds}>
            {turn.reasoning}
          </ChatReasoning>
        )}
        {turn.tools.map((tool) => (
          <ChatTool key={tool.id} name={tool.name} status={tool.status}
            input={tool.input} output={tool.output} />
        ))}
        <ChatResponse streaming={turn.streaming}>{turn.text}</ChatResponse>
        <ChatSources sources={turn.sources} />
      </ChatMessage>
    ),
  )}
</ChatThread>
<ChatComposer
  running={running}
  onStop={stop}
  onSubmit={({ text, files }) => send(text, files)}
  commands={[{ value: "summarize", label: "summarize", description: "Shorten the thread" }]}
  mentions={projectFiles.map((f) => ({ value: f.path, label: f.name }))}
  attachments={{ accept: "image/*,.pdf", maxFiles: 5, maxSize: 10 * 1024 * 1024 }}
  tools={
    <>
      <ChatModelPicker models={models} value={model} onValueChange={setModel} />
      <ChatUsage used={used} limit={200000} />
    </>
  }
/>
```

- `ChatThread`'s `label` ("Conversation") names its scroll region, which holds a
  `role="log"`. The region is capped at `--chat-thread-height` (26rem by default).
- `ChatMessage` takes `from` (`"user"`, `"assistant"` or `"system"`), `name` (You,
  Assistant or System by default), `avatar` (`{ src?, fallback }`, named by `name`) and
  `time` (a `Date`, shown in the viewer's short time format). `streaming` marks it
  `aria-busy` and draws a caret after the last block.
- `ChatMessageActions` shows Copy when `text` is given, Retry with `onRetry`, Edit with
  `onEdit`, and Good and Bad with `onFeedbackChange`. Pressing the pressed one again gives
  `null`. Copy announces "Copied". The toolbar and its Good and Bad group are named with
  the message's first words, as each button is (`Actions: "Here's a summary of the…"`,
  `Feedback: "Here's a summary of the…"`); `label` gives the toolbar a name of your own.
- `ChatBranch` takes `index` (from 0), `count` and `onIndexChange`, and renders nothing for
  fewer than two versions. "2 of 3" is announced as it changes.
- `ChatTasks` takes `tasks` (`{ id, title, status, detail? }`), `title` ("Plan") and
  `defaultOpen` (on). Statuses `pending`, `running`, `done` and `failed` read as To do,
  In progress, Done and Failed.

## Answers

- `ChatResponse` takes the Markdown as its child, with GitHub tables, task lists and
  strikethrough. With `streaming`, half-written Markdown is completed (remend), so
  `**bold` shows as bold, not stars.
- Raw HTML in the Markdown is dropped, never rendered: model output is untrusted. `http`
  and `https` links open in a new tab and say so to screen readers. Wide tables scroll in
  a focusable region.
- Images in an answer load when they're same-origin, `data:` or `blob:`. Any other image
  shows as a link ("Image: chart"), because its address could carry what the model read
  to another server. `allowImage(url)` returns `true` for the ones to load.
- Fenced code with a language is highlighted by shiki, loaded the first time it's needed,
  one language at a time, in the skin's colors. A language shiki doesn't know shows as
  plain text. Each block has a Wrap toggle and a Copy button named "Copy ts". Render
  `ChatCodeBlock` yourself with `code`, `language` and `filename` (which then names the
  block and its Copy button).
- `ChatReasoning` opens while `streaming` is on and closes when it ends, unless a person
  or an agent opened or closed it; then it stays as they left it. It reads "Thinking…"
  while streaming, "Thought for 4s" with `seconds` (rounded, at least 1), and
  "Reasoning" without.
- `ChatTool`'s `status` is `pending`, `running`, `approval`, `done`, `error` or `denied`,
  read as Queued, Running, Needs your approval, Done, Failed and Not allowed. It opens
  itself for `approval` and `error` unless you pass `defaultOpen`. `title` replaces
  `name` in the header; `input` and `output` show as JSON (strings as they are); `error`
  shows in place of the output.
- `ChatTool` has no Allow or Deny buttons of its own. Put yours in its `children`, which
  render in the panel, and give Allow a `data-agent-confirm` (the web element does).
- `ChatSources` takes `sources` (`{ href, title, description? }`) and renders nothing for
  an empty list. `ChatCitation` takes `index` and one `source`: a link named "Source 1:
  title" whose hover card shows the title, host and description.
- `ChatImage` needs `src`, `alt`, `width` and `height`, so the space is held before it
  loads; `caption` is optional.

## The composer

- `onSubmit({ text, files })` gets the trimmed text and the attached files, then the box
  clears. With no text and no files, nothing is sent.
- While `running` is on, Enter and Send don't send. With `onStop` too, Send becomes Stop.
- `commands` show after "/" at the start of the message and `mentions` after "@", each
  `{ value, label, description? }`. Choosing one inserts the trigger and the label
  ("/summarize "); `onSubmit` gets that text, not the item's `value`.
- `attachments` is off by default. `{ accept?, maxFiles?, maxSize? }` (`maxSize` in bytes)
  adds a paperclip, takes files dropped on the box or pasted into it, and lists them as
  chips with Remove. UI SDK's `FileInput` announces files it rejects; they never join.
- `tools` render in the composer's toolbar, beside Send. `label` ("Message") names the
  box; `placeholder` defaults to "Message…".
- Up brings back messages sent from this box since it mounted.
- `ChatModelPicker` takes `models` (`{ value, label, description? }`), `value` or
  `defaultValue` (the first model when neither is given), `onValueChange` and `label`
  ("Model", visually hidden).
- `ChatUsage` takes `used` and `limit`, with `unit` ("tokens") and `label` ("Context
  used"). The meter carries `data-level="medium"` past 70% and `"high"` past 90%.

## Chats and the launcher

- `ChatThreadList` takes `threads` (`{ id, title, updatedAt? }`), `value` (the open chat,
  marked `aria-current="page"`) and `onValueChange(id)`. `label` names the list ("Chats").
- `onNew` adds New chat. `onRename(id, title)` and `onDelete(id)` add a "More for
  title" menu to each chat. Rename edits in place: Enter or leaving the field saves,
  Escape cancels, and an empty or unchanged title isn't sent. Delete asks in an alert
  dialog ("Delete “Launch plan”?") before calling `onDelete`.
- `updatedAt` shows as "4 min ago" and is the chat button's description. It's worked out
  when the list renders, not kept current.
- `ChatLauncher` takes `label` ("Open assistant"), `title` ("Assistant") and the panel's
  `children`. The panel opens above its button and stays open while you click around
  the page; Escape, the button and Close shut it.

## The chat-app template

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @uiset/chat-app
```

`<ChatAppTemplate assistant={assistant} />` is the kit as a page. `assistant` is an async
generator given `{ text, files, model, history, signal }` that yields `text`, `reasoning`,
`reasoning-end`, `tool` (the same `id` updates the card) and `sources` events; the sample
one streams a placeholder. It also takes `models`, `commands`, `mentions`, `suggestions`,
`userName` ("You"), `userAvatar` and `limit` (200000, for the usage meter).

- It runs one answer at a time. Stop aborts `signal` and isn't shown as a failure; any
  other error adds "The answer stopped early. Try again."
- It starts on the second entry in `models` (the sample's "Balanced").
- New chats are numbered ("Untitled chat 2") until the first message, cut to 40
  characters, becomes the title. Deleting the last chat starts a new one.
- Retry sends the question before that answer again, as a new turn.
- Usage is an estimate per chat (`estimateTokens`: 900 plus 4 per character of each
  message sent), until your model reports its own.

[Connecting a model to the chat app template](./templates.md#connecting-a-model-to-chat-app) shows one connected.

## Keys

| Keys                    | Where                      | Does                                                   |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Enter                   | message box                | Send; with a "/" or "@" menu open, choose the item     |
| Shift+Enter             | message box                | A new line                                             |
| Up, Down                | message box                | What you sent before, when the caret is on the first or last line |
| "/" at the start, "@"   | message box                | Commands, mentions: arrows move, Enter or Tab choose, Escape closes |
| Tab                     | thread, code, tables       | A stop while it scrolls and holds nothing else to press; arrows and Page keys scroll it |
| Arrows                  | message actions, suggestions | Move along the toolbar (one Tab stop)               |
| Enter, Space            | reasoning, tool, sources, plan | Open or close it                                   |
| Enter, Escape           | rename field               | Save, cancel (leaving the field saves too)             |
| Escape                  | launcher                   | Close it                                               |

Enter doesn't send while an input method is composing. Copying, version changes and
attached or rejected files are announced.

## For agents

The bridge sees UI SDK components, so messages themselves aren't in its snapshot: give
your agent the conversation from your own state. What it does see, by name:

- **Message box:** a trigger menu named by `label` ("Message") with `insert`, plus Send
  (or Stop) and "Attach files" (`setValue`, `addFiles`, `removeFile`, `clear`, `open`).
  `insert` writes only while the box has focus; without focus it reports success and
  writes nothing. There's no `setValue` on the box.
- **Toolbar:** "Model" is a select an agent sets by a model's label or value; "Context
  used" is a meter it reads (`value`, `min`, `max`).
- **Answers:** each reasoning, tool call, sources list and plan is a collapsible named by
  its header ("Thought for 4s", "Searched the docs, Done", "Used 2 sources"), with
  `setOpen`. Each message's actions are a toolbar (`Actions: "Here's a summary of the…"`)
  to `press` Copy message, Retry message, Edit message, Good response or Bad response,
  each named with its message's first words so an agent can tell one reply's from
  another's (`Copy message: "Here's a summary of the…"`); the feedback group
  (`Feedback: "Here's a summary of the…"`) also takes `setValue`. Code blocks have "Wrap lines" and "Copy ts"; citations are hover cards
  ("Source 1: AbortController").
- **Chats:** New chat, each chat as a button named by its title, and "More for title" to
  `press` Rename or Delete. Rename shows a "Rename title" field; an agent's `setValue`
  fills it, but it's saved only on Enter or when focus leaves it.
- **Delete chat** in the dialog carries `data-agent-confirm` ("Deletes the chat
  “Launch plan” and its messages"), so a step on it waits for the person, or fails with
  "Needs a person" when the bridge has no `allow`.

A few names still repeat from one answer to the next: a code block's "Wrap lines" and a
reply's "Previous version". With two on the page, a step that names one fails and lists
the refs; retry with a ref. Nothing in the kit is `data-agent-hidden`.

## Web Components

`<uiset-chat>`, `<uiset-chat-composer>`, `<uiset-chat-threads>`,
`<uiset-chat-model-picker>` and `<uiset-chat-usage>` are the kit as custom elements.
`<uiset-chat>` draws a whole conversation from AI SDK's `messages` shape, with Allow and
Deny on tool calls that wait for approval. The launcher has no element. See
[Web Components](./web-components.md#chat).


<!-- docs/data-grid.md -->

# Data Grid

A grid for real data, built on UI SDK: thousands of rows, spreadsheet keys, editing in
place, and actions an agent can call. One item, `data-grid`, gives you `DataGrid`,
`DataGridToolbar` and the framework-free pieces under them.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @uiset/data-grid
```

## Why it's built this way

UI SDK ships the hard behaviors a grid needs, and the grid is those behaviors wired
together, not a rewrite of them:

| Need                                         | UI SDK piece                       |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| One tab stop, arrows, Home/End, Page keys    | `createGridFocus`                  |
| Select a block, rows or columns; copy it     | `createCellRange`, `textToCells`   |
| Edit in place: Enter, F2, typing, Escape     | `createInlineEdit`                 |
| Choose from a column's `options`             | `Combobox`                         |
| Render 10,000 rows, reveal one off screen    | `createVirtualizer`                |
| Column menu, View menu, filters, grouping    | `Menu`, `Popover`, `Select`        |
| Drag a column edge                           | `bindDrag`                         |
| Announce sorts, counts and edits             | `announce`                         |
| Agents sort, filter, select and edit         | the primitive's `agent` key        |

Sorting, filtering, grouping and CSV export are plain functions in `data-grid/view.ts`,
so they run on a server or in a worker too.

## Use

```tsx
import { DataGrid, DataGridToolbar, type DataGridColumn } from "@/components/ui/data-grid"

const columns: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { id: "id", header: "Order", value: (o) => o.id, pinned: true, hideable: false },
  { id: "customer", header: "Customer", value: (o) => o.customer, editable: true },
  { id: "status", header: "Status", value: (o) => o.status, options: ["Paid", "Pending"], editable: true },
  {
    id: "amount",
    header: "Amount",
    type: "number",
    value: (o) => o.amount,
    text: (o) => money.format(o.amount),
    editable: true,
  },
  { id: "rush", header: "Rush", type: "boolean", value: (o) => o.rush, editable: true },
]

<DataGrid
  label="Orders"
  rows={orders}
  columns={columns}
  getRowId={(o) => o.id}
  selectable
  onCellEdit={({ rowId, column, value }) => save(rowId, column, value)}
  persist="orders-grid"
  height="30rem"
>
  <DataGridToolbar filename="orders" selectionActions={<Button>Mark paid</Button>} />
</DataGrid>
```

- `value` is what sorts and filters; `text` is what shows and copies; `render` replaces
  what shows (a badge, a link) without changing either.
- `type` sets how an edit is read, with UI SDK's `parseNumber` and `parseDate` in
  `locale`: `"number"` follows the locale's grouping and accepts a currency sign
  (`$1,200.50`) but refuses words (`12 units`); `"date"` reads "Nov 20", "2026-11-20" or
  the locale's order and stores that calendar day; `"boolean"` flips with Space.
  `options` limits an edit to a list. Its editor is UI SDK's Combobox in the cell: the
  list opens under the cell in the skin's own style, typing narrows it, and only an
  option can be saved. Pasted and agent edits are checked against the list too.
- `onCellEdit` gets the parsed value. Return `false` to keep the editor open. Without
  it, nothing is editable.
- `sort`, `query`, `filters`, `groupBy`, `selected`, `columnState` and `density` can
  each be controlled (keep filters in the URL, say), with a `default…` and an
  `on…Change`.
- Pass `locale` when rendering on a server, so counts format the same on both sides.
- `persist` saves column order, widths, visibility, pinning and density in
  `localStorage`, read after the first render so server markup matches.

## Toolbar parts

`DataGridToolbar` is one arrangement of parts you can use on their own, anywhere inside
a `DataGrid`: `DataGridSearch`, `DataGridFilters`, `DataGridGroupBy`, `DataGridViewMenu`,
`DataGridExport` and `DataGridSelection` (the count, your bulk actions, Clear selection).
`useDataGrid()` gives a custom part the same state.

```tsx
<DataGrid label="Orders" rows={orders} columns={columns} getRowId={(o) => o.id} selectable>
  <div className="my-toolbar">
    <DataGridSearch />
    <DataGridSelection>
      <Button>Mark paid</Button>
    </DataGridSelection>
    <DataGridExport filename="orders" />
  </div>
</DataGrid>
```

## Keys

| Keys                           | Where         | Does                                         |
| ------------------------------ | ------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Arrows, Home, End, Page keys   | anywhere      | Move one cell, to the row's ends, by a page  |
| Control+Home, Control+End      | anywhere      | First cell, last cell (rows render on the way) |
| Enter, Space                   | header        | Sort ascending, descending, off              |
| Shift+Enter                    | header        | Add the column to the sort                   |
| Shift+F10 or the Menu key      | header        | Column menu: sort, group, pin, move, hide    |
| Alt+Left, Alt+Right            | header        | Narrower, wider (Option on a Mac)            |
| Alt+Shift+Left, Alt+Shift+Right | header       | Move the column                              |
| Enter, F2, or start typing     | editable cell | Edit; Enter saves, Escape cancels, Tab saves |
| Up, Down, or keep typing       | a list cell's editor | Move through the options, or narrow them; Enter or Tab saves the highlighted one |
| Space                          | yes/no cell   | Flip it                                      |
| Space                          | first column  | Check the row                                |
| Enter                          | group row     | Open or close the group                      |
| Shift+Arrows, Shift+click      | anywhere      | Select a block                               |
| Shift+Space, Control+Space     | anywhere      | Select the rows, the columns                 |
| Control+A, Escape              | anywhere      | Select all cells, clear the block            |
| Control+C, Control+V           | anywhere      | Copy the block; paste into editable cells    |

The grid's description lists these for screen reader users, and every sort, resize,
move, paste and filter result is announced. Each header also has a column menu button
for pointers, touch and touch screen readers (it never takes the tab stop), and the menu
has **Wider** and **Narrower**, so resizing never needs a drag.

## For agents

The grid offers `sortBy`, `filter`, `filterColumn`, `selectRows`, `clearSelection`,
`editCell`, `groupBy` and `showColumn`. Columns are named by header and rows by their id
or first column, the way a person reads them. The snapshot shows what the grid is doing
(rows shown, sort, filter, grouping, selection), and `query` returns every row, including
the ones not rendered.

A step that can't run says why, so the agent can try again:

```txt
No column "Total" in Orders. Its columns: Order, Customer, Region, Status, Amount, Placed, Rush.
Amount needs a number
Status must be one of Paid, Pending, Refunded, Failed
```

Edits go through the same parsing and `onCellEdit` as a person's, so your validation
applies to both.

## Accessibility notes

- `role="grid"` with `aria-rowcount` and `aria-rowindex`, so screen readers know the
  full size while only visible rows render.
- The primary sort column carries `aria-sort`. Group cells carry `aria-expanded` (a grid
  row may not; only a treegrid's can).
- Row checkboxes are real checkboxes that never take focus; the cell keeps it, so the
  arrows keep working after a click. Shift-click ranges follow the rows on screen.
- The editor covers its cell, says what's wrong with `aria-invalid` and a message, and
  announces it.
- Range outlines follow the reading direction, and the focused cell's ring is an outline,
  so both hold in right-to-left and in forced colors.

## Limits, for now

- Rows have one height per density; wrapping text is cut with an ellipsis.
- Columns aren't virtualized; hundreds of columns will be slow.
- Find in page only finds rendered rows; use the search box. `createVirtualizer`'s
  `findable` can lift this later.


<!-- docs/charts.md -->

# Charts: design plan

Step 4 of the owner's plan. UI SDK ships no charts, and a dashboard is the first thing
most apps build, so this is a gap a UI SDK developer hits on day one.

## The set (complete-set rule)

What a developer needs to ship dashboards and reports end to end:

| Item            | What it is                                                                  |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `chart`         | The frame every chart shares: title, description, legend, Chart/Table switch, tooltip, scales, palette tokens per skin |
| `line-chart`    | Trend over time; one or more series; area wash for one series; stacked areas |
| `bar-chart`     | Compare categories; vertical or horizontal; grouped or stacked; ranked       |
| `scatter-chart` | Two measures per item; up to three series; nearest-point hover               |
| `heatmap`       | Magnitude on a grid (weekday × hour, day calendar); one hue, scale legend    |
| `segmented-bar` | One whole split into parts, tall (with values) or thin (beside figures)      |
| `sparkline`     | A trend inside text, a table cell or a stat                                  |
| Stat with trend | The existing `stat` gains `delta` direction and a `trend` sparkline          |

No pie or donut. Part-to-whole is a segmented bar (at a glance) or ranked bars (to
compare); the docs say why, so nobody thinks it was forgotten.

## Principles (from the dataviz method, applied to UISet)

- **Form before color.** Every chart's docs start with the job it does.
- **One axis.** No dual-axis option, ever. Two measures → two charts.
- **Color follows the entity.** Series get slots by their place in `series`, so
  isolating or hiding one never repaints the others. There are eight slots; a ninth
  series and beyond draw in the "Other" gray, so fold your tail into one "Other" series.
- **Thin marks.** Bars ≤ 24px with a 4px rounded data end, square at the baseline; 2px
  lines with round joins; markers ≥ 8px with a 2px surface ring; area wash ~10%;
  hairline solid grid and axes, never dashed; 2px surface gap between touching fills.
- **Labels in ink, never series color.** Identity rides a swatch or line key beside it.
  Direct labels only at line ends (≤ 4 series) and bar tips where they fit.
- **Legend for two or more series**, and it doubles as a filter: pressing a legend
  entry isolates or hides a series (toggle buttons, `aria-pressed`).
- **Every chart has a table twin.** A Chart/Table switch shows the same data as a real
  `<table>`. Tooltips enhance; they never gate.
- **Hover and focus show the same thing.** Line/area: a crosshair snaps to the nearest
  x and the tooltip lists every series there. Bars, cells, dots: the mark is the
  target, at least 24px, and lifts on hover.

## Keyboard and screen readers

The SVG is drawing only (`aria-hidden`). Over it sits an HTML layer of hit targets, one
per data position (an x for lines, a bar, a cell, a point), which is what people and
assistive tech use:

- The layer is a `listbox` with one tab stop, from UI SDK's roving focus with a custom
  `move`: arrows follow the chart's direction (`aria-orientation` says which), and in a
  heatmap Up and Down move a row and stop at the edges. Home and End jump. Charts draw
  left to right in every language, so Right is always the next position.
- Each target is an `option` whose name is the full reading: "March 3: Revenue $12,400,
  Costs $8,100". Selecting one pins it (and is a cross-filter hook: `onSelect`).
- Moving announces nothing extra: the option's name is the announcement.
- Targets are the hit areas for the pointer too, so hover and focus share one code path
  and the hit area is the whole band, never a 2px line.

## For agents

Each chart is a UI SDK primitive with an `agent` key: `items` returns the data as rows,
so `query` can answer "what was revenue in March?" without a screenshot, and actions
`isolate`, `showAll`, `showTable` and `select` let an agent drive the view. `select` takes
what people read ("March") before a key. The Chart/Table switch is hidden from agents while
the chart shows, since `showTable` does its job; with the table showing, the chart's actions
are out of reach, so the switch is open to agents as the way back.

## Color per skin (validated, not eyeballed)

Tokens: `--chart-1` … `--chart-8` (categorical), `--chart-seq-1` … `-7` (sequential, one
hue), `--chart-neg`/`--chart-mid`/`--chart-pos` (diverging), plus grid, axis and ink.
Each skin sets them; base.css draws with them.

| Skin, scheme         | Surface   | Palette                                              | Result |
| -------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| Base, light          | `#fdfdff` | reference light set                                  | all gates pass; aqua, yellow, magenta < 3:1 → relief: direct labels + table view |
| Base, dark           | `#0e0f13` | reference dark set                                   | all gates pass, all ≥ 3:1 |
| Studio (dark only)   | `#34383e` | reference dark set                                   | all gates pass; magenta, green < 3:1 → same relief |
| Blueprint (dark only) | `#053d75` | `#9da3ef #73edb1 #fd8537 #f55fad #fed917 #ffc4fe #b2e37e #73c3ff` | adjacent CVD 14.6, normal 18.7; first six all-pairs CVD 9.3, normal 17.3; all ≥ 3:1 |

The gates are the validator's: adjacent pairs, which is what bars and lines need. Pairs
that aren't neighbors can still be close in the reference sets (light pink and orange,
dark green and pink under deutan vision), so charts never lean on color alone: a scatter
chart's series differ in shape, a segmented bar labels its parts, and every chart has its
table. Blueprint's first six clear every pair as well, since its mid-blue paper leaves
less room between colors. `tests/unit/chart-palette.test.ts` measures them, so a re-picked
color that brings back a lookalike pair fails.

Blueprint's set sits above the validator's dark lightness band (0.48–0.67) on purpose:
the band assumes a near-black surface, and on mid-blue paper (L 0.36) colors inside it
fall under 3:1. Contrast is the check the band stands in for, and it passes.

## Look

Charts take the skin. Base: quiet hairlines and the palette. Blueprint: the skin's
white linework for axes, grid and crosshair, and its light colored-pencil set. Studio: the
amber lamp as the crosshair and the sequential ramp.

## Use

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @uiset/line-chart @uiset/bar-chart \
  @uiset/scatter-chart @uiset/heatmap \
  @uiset/segmented-bar @uiset/sparkline
```

Every chart takes `title` (its name for people and agents), `data`, and accessors.
`format` formats values in tooltips, labels and the table.

```tsx
<LineChart
  title="Revenue and costs"
  description="2026, by month"
  data={months}
  x={(d) => d.month}
  series={[
    { key: "revenue", label: "Revenue", value: (d) => d.revenue },
    { key: "costs", label: "Costs", value: (d) => d.costs },
  ]}
  format={(n) => money.format(n)}
/>

<BarChart title="Revenue by region" data={regions} x={(d) => d.region}
  series={[{ key: "revenue", label: "Revenue", value: (d) => d.revenue }]}
  orientation="horizontal" sort="descending" />

<SegmentedBar title="Traffic sources" parts={[{ key: "search", label: "Search", value: 189000 }, …]} />

<Heatmap title="Sessions by day and hour" data={sessions} rows={days} columns={hours}
  row={(d) => d.day} column={(d) => d.hour} value={(d) => d.sessions} measure="Sessions" />

<ScatterChart title="Deal size and time to close" data={deals} label={(d) => d.name}
  x={(d) => d.days} y={(d) => d.size} xLabel="Days to close" yLabel="Deal size" />

<Stat label="Revenue" value="$91,000" change={{ value: "9.6%", direction: "up" }}
  trend={lastTwelveMonths} />
```

`Sparkline` and `Stat` hold no state, so they render in a Server Component.

```tsx
<LineChart title="Visits by channel" layout="stacked" data={…} x={…} series={…} />
```

- `LineChart`: `layout` is `"line"`, `"area"` (a wash under each line) or `"stacked"`
  (areas to a total, whose readings and table include the total); `zero` keeps zero on
  the axis (default on). Stacks with negative layers stay inside the plot.
- `BarChart`: `orientation` (`"vertical"` columns or `"horizontal"` bars), `layout`
  (`"grouped"` or `"stacked"`), `sort`, `labels`.
- `ScatterChart`: `series` takes up to three groups, each with a `match`.
- `SegmentedBar`: `variant="thin"` for an 8px bar beside its figures.
- `selected` / `onSelect` pin a data position from outside, for cross-filtering a
  dashboard: select a month in one chart, filter the others. Keys are the datum's index
  in `data`, however a bar chart sorts it. `onSelect(key, { source, reason })` says who
  pinned it (`keyboard`, `pointer`, `agent`) and why; when new data drops the pinned
  position, it fires once with `null` and `{ source: "data", reason: "removed" }`. A
  controlled `selected` that the page doesn't change refuses the pin.
- `locale` formats axis ticks, readings and shares; pass it when rendering on a server
  so the server and the browser print the same digits.
- `ChartFrame` is exported for charts of your own: compute the drawing and the data
  positions, and it supplies the rest.

## Keys

| Keys                    | Does                                               |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab                     | Into the chart (one stop) and out again            |
| Left, Right (Up, Down)  | The next data position; bar charts on their side use Up and Down |
| Up, Down in a heatmap   | The cell above or below                            |
| Home, End               | The first or last position                         |
| Enter, Space            | Pin the position (and its tooltip); again to unpin |
| Escape                  | Unpin; with nothing pinned, dismiss the tooltip    |

Each position's name is its full reading, so moving is announcing: "Aug: Revenue
$70,000, Costs $52,000".


<!-- docs/board.md -->

# Board

A kanban board on UI SDK's `createTransfer`: cards in columns that people move with the
pointer, the keyboard or an agent, with the same rules and announcements for all three.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @uiset/board
```

## Use

```tsx
const [board] = useState(createBoardController)

<BoardToolbar label="Cards" query={query} onQueryChange={setQuery}
  people={people} person={person} onPersonChange={setPerson} />
<Board
  label="Sprint board"
  controller={board}
  columns={[
    { id: "todo", title: "To do" },
    { id: "doing", title: "In progress", limit: 3 },
    { id: "done", title: "Done" },
  ]}
  cards={cards}
  lanes={lanes}
  onLanesChange={(next, { key, from, to, index }) => setLanes(next)}
  onCardOpen={setOpen}
  onAddCard={(column, title) => add(column, title) /* return the new card's id */}
  filter={(card) => matches(card, query, person)}
/>
<BoardCardDialog board={board} card={open} column={columnOf(open)} columns={columns}
  people={people} labels={labels}
  onSave={save} onDelete={remove} onClose={() => setOpen(null)} />
```

- `lanes` maps each column to its card ids, in order. `cards` holds the cards by id.
- A column's `limit` refuses cards past it, for people (the move skips to the next
  column with room), for drags, and for agents (with a reason).
- `filter` hides cards that don't match without moving them; focus skips them, and the
  board's one tab stop never stays on a hidden card. While a filter hides cards, nothing
  moves: a carried card would step through cards nobody can see. Space says so.
- `onAddCard` returns the new card's id. A controlled board's owner adds it to `lanes`; an
  uncontrolled board adds it itself. When it fills the column, focus goes to the new card.
- `controller` (from `createBoardController()`) connects `BoardCardDialog`, or your code, to
  the board: `moveCard`, `addCard`, `hasRoom`, `focusCard`, `cardElement`, `neighbor`. The
  dialog moves cards through it, so a move keeps column limits, reaches `onLanesChange`
  (and your Undo toast), and focus goes back to the card, or to its neighbor after a
  delete or an edit the filter hides.
- `BoardCardDialog` edits the assignee only when given `people`, and labels only when given
  `labels`; labels it doesn't list are kept. Full columns are listed but can't be chosen.
- `renderCard` replaces the card face; `BoardCardFace` is the default. `describeCard`
  gives screen readers the details after the title (priority, due date, person and
  labels by default).
- `locked` marks cards that can't move. `messages` replaces the help, empty, full and
  filtered copy; `moveMessage` replaces the move announcements (for other languages).
- `today` marks overdue cards; pass the real date.
- `BoardToolbar`'s `label` says what the board holds, like "Cards" or "Issues": it names
  the search ("Search cards") and the group ("Cards tools"). Give it a word other than the
  board's own name, or a step by the board's name finds the search too.

## Touch

A finger scrolls the board from anywhere on a card, and drags it from the grip at its
top corner, which shows on touch screens only. The keyboard and agents don't need it.

## Known limits

Releasing a dragged card over a full column, or outside the board, drops it in the last
column it passed that had room. That's UI SDK's `createTransfer` (reported upstream).

## Keys

| Keys                    | Does                                                         |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Tab                     | Into the board (one stop) and out                            |
| Up, Down, Home, End     | Cards in a column                                            |
| Left, Right             | The card at the same height in the next column with cards    |
| Space                   | Pick a card up; arrows carry it; Space drops it              |
| Escape                  | Put a carried card back                                      |
| Enter                   | Open the card's details: edit, move to a column, delete      |

Every pickup, move and drop is announced ("Write the spec, moved to Doing, position 2 of
3"). Cards are options in a listbox per column, with `aria-roledescription` "card" and
"column", the way UI SDK's sortable lists describe themselves; the carried card is the
selected one.

## For agents

`moveCard(card, column, position?)`, `addCard(column, title)` and `openCard(card)`, by the
titles people see. The snapshot's items list every card with its column, assignee and due
date. A board without `onCardOpen` or `onAddCard` tells agents it can't open or add cards.
Deleting goes through the dialog's confirm, marked `data-agent-confirm`.


<!-- docs/scheduler.md -->

# Scheduler

Calendars on UI SDK's `createSpans`: events people draw, move and resize with the
pointer or the keyboard, on a week, a day, or a timeline of rooms.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @uiset/scheduler
```

## Parts

| Part               | What it is                                                                 |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Schedule`         | Tracks of events: days down a week (`axis="y"`), or rooms across a day (`axis="x"`) |
| `MonthView`        | A month on UI SDK's Calendar; each day lists its events; choosing a day opens it |
| `SchedulerToolbar` | Today, previous and next, the range shown, the view, New event           |
| `EventDialog`      | Create or edit: title, day, start, end, where; Delete asks first          |
| `createScheduleController` | Connects `EventDialog` (or your code) to a `Schedule`: its rules and its focus |

## Use

```tsx
const [schedule] = useState(createScheduleController)

<SchedulerToolbar title="Nov 16 – 22, 2026" view={view} onViewChange={setView} unit="week"
  onToday={…} onPrevious={…} onNext={…} onNewEvent={() => setOpen(draft)} />
<Schedule
  label="Team calendar"
  controller={schedule}
  tracks={days.map((d) => ({ id: d, label: longDate(d), short: shortDate(d) }))}
  events={events}
  onEventsChange={(next, { action, id }) => setEvents(next)}
  onEventOpen={setOpen}
  startHour={8}
  endHour={19}
  step={15}
  now={new Date()}
  timeZone="America/Los_Angeles"
  today={todayIso}
/>
<EventDialog schedule={schedule} startHour={8} endHour={19} step={15}
  event={open} tracks={tracks} onSave={save} onDelete={remove} onClose={() => setOpen(null)} />
```

- An event is `{ id, track, start, end, title, color?, location? }`; `start` and `end` are
  minutes from midnight, `track` is a day (an ISO date) or a room id.
- `overlap={false}` refuses bookings that collide, for every kind of input. With overlaps
  allowed, events share the day's width in lanes (`stackSpans`).
- `onCreate(span)` makes the event a draw or click creates; return `null` to refuse.
- `locked(event)` keeps an event from changing, for people and agents.
- **Time zones.** `start` and `end` are wall-clock minutes in the zone the schedule shows,
  and `track` is that zone's date. `now` is read in `timeZone` (the viewer's by default),
  so the current-time line and `today` agree. Convert stored instants to the zone at the
  edge; a 9:00 event stays at 9:00 across a daylight-saving change.
- `EventDialog` with the controller keeps the schedule's rules (hours, steps, overlaps)
  and says why a time won't do, on the field that's wrong. Focus goes back to the saved
  event, or to the next event once one is deleted.
- `size` is how long a click on an empty stretch makes an event. `renderEvent` replaces an
  event's face; `timeLabel` changes how times read (24-hour, other languages);
  `MonthView` takes `locale` and `timeLabel` too.
- On touch screens a finger scrolls the schedule; a tap makes an event, and events drag.

## Keys

| Keys                       | Does                                      |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Tab                        | Each event, in time order                 |
| Up, Down (Left, Right on a timeline) | Earlier or later by the step    |
| Left, Right (Up, Down on a timeline) | The previous or next day or room |
| Shift with those arrows    | Change when it ends                       |
| Delete, Backspace          | Remove it (the demo offers Undo)          |
| Enter, Space               | Open it (each event is a button)          |

New events by keyboard come from **New event**. Every move, resize and removal is
announced. Delete hands focus to the next event, or to the schedule when none is left.
Choosing a day in the month focuses that day's first event. In the month view each day is named with its events ("Wednesday, November
18, 2026, 2 events: Standup at 9:00 AM, Launch rehearsal at 3:00 PM").

## For agents

`addEvent(day, start, end, title)`, `moveEvent(event, day, start)`,
`resizeEvent(event, end)` and `openEvent(event)`, with times as `HH:MM` and days by name
("Tuesday"). They keep the same rules a drag does, and a time that doesn't fit says why.
Events are named by title or id; when two share a title, the error lists both with their
ids. The snapshot lists each event as `{ value: id, label: "Standup, Monday, …" }`.
Deleting goes through the dialog's confirm (`data-agent-confirm`), so a person approves
it; `removeEvent` stays on the API for your own code.


<!-- docs/canvas.md -->

# Canvas

A node editor composed from UI SDK's canvas behaviors: `createViewport` pans and zooms,
`createMove` drags nodes, `createSelection` and `createLasso` choose them, `spatialMove`
sends focus to the nearest node, and `createConnect` draws wires. People use a pointer or
the keyboard; agents use the same actions by the names people see.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @uiset/canvas
```

## Parts

| Part                     | What it is                                                                       |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Canvas`                 | The editor: dot grid, nodes with ports, wires, zoom controls and a minimap       |
| `CanvasToolbar`          | On UI SDK's Toolbar: Add node (by kind), remove the selection, undo, redo, fit view |
| `CanvasInspector`        | The selected node: rename it, list its wires with Disconnect, and your own fields |
| `useCanvasHistory`       | Nodes and edges with undo and redo; one step per move, add, wire or removal      |
| `createCanvasController` | Connects the toolbar, inspector or your code to the canvas                       |

## Use

```tsx
const [canvas] = useState(createCanvasController)
const history = useCanvasHistory({ nodes, edges })
const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>([])

<CanvasToolbar canvas={canvas} kinds={kinds} selectedCount={selected.length}
  onUndo={history.undo} onRedo={history.redo} canUndo={history.canUndo} canRedo={history.canRedo} />
<Canvas
  label="Workflow"
  controller={canvas}
  nodes={history.nodes}
  edges={history.edges}
  onNodesChange={history.onNodesChange}
  onEdgesChange={history.onEdgesChange}
  selected={selected}
  onSelectedChange={setSelected}
  kinds={kinds}
  onAddNode={(kind, at, title) => ({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), kind, title: title ?? "New step", ...at, ...portsFor(kind) })}
  renderNode={(node) => node.data?.summary}
  onUndo={history.undo}
  onRedo={history.redo}
  fitView
/>
<CanvasInspector node={one(selected)} nodes={history.nodes} edges={history.edges} canvas={canvas}
  onRename={rename}>{(node) => <YourFields node={node} />}</CanvasInspector>
```

- A node is `{ id, title, x, y, inputs?, outputs?, kind?, color?, width?, data? }`; a port is
  `{ id, label }`. Ids may not contain `:`.
- An edge is `{ id, from, to }`, with ports keyed `"node:out:port"` and `"node:in:port"`.
  Wires run from an output to an input on another node; each input takes one wire, and a
  new one replaces it. `canConnect(from, to)` adds your own rules, like matching types.
- Nodes, edges and the selection are controlled or not (`defaultNodes`, `defaultEdges`,
  `defaultSelected`). Removing nodes removes their wires.
- `renderNode` draws under a node's ports, as text or pictures: node faces aren't
  interactive, so the nodes can be a listbox. Its text is part of the node's description.
  Put fields in the inspector: its children start over for each node shown.
- A node is named by its title, then its kind, as it reads on screen; its description adds
  the body and its wires.
- `CanvasToolbar`'s `label` is its own name, "Canvas tools" by default. Keep the canvas's
  name out of it: agents find components by names that contain what they ask for.
- `grid` is where dropped nodes snap and how far Alt with an arrow moves them (8).
- `locked(node)` keeps a node in place. `fitView` frames every node on first show;
  `controls` and `minimap` turn the corner parts off.
- Ports are drawn from fixed sizes (a 36px header and 28px rows, in canvas units), so wires
  never wait on measuring. Keep custom styles to those sizes.

## Keys

| Keys                        | Does                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab                         | Into the canvas (one stop, on the last node focused) and out           |
| Arrows                      | The nearest node in that direction                                     |
| Alt with arrows             | Move the node (or the selection) by the grid; Shift for ten steps      |
| Space                       | Select or unselect the node                                            |
| Ctrl/⌘ A, Escape            | Select every node; clear the selection                                 |
| C                           | Start a wire from the node's output (C again: its next output)         |
| Arrows, Enter, Escape       | While wiring: choose an input, connect, stop                           |
| Delete, Backspace           | Remove the node, or the selection; focus moves to the nearest node     |
| Enter                       | Open the node (your `onNodeOpen`, like focusing the inspector)         |
| +, −, 0                     | Zoom in, out, back to 100%                                             |
| Ctrl/⌘ Z, Ctrl/⌘ Shift Z    | Undo, redo (with `onUndo` and `onRedo`)                                |

Focus never falls to the page: removing a node (by Delete, the toolbar, an undo or an
agent) moves it to the nearest node, the toolbar keeps disabled tools focusable, and
Disconnect in the inspector moves to the next wire. A node added from the toolbar takes
focus; one an agent adds doesn't take it from the person. Focus rings and the selection
edge keep their width on screen at any zoom.

With a pointer: drag empty space to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom, Shift-drag to select a
box, drag a node (or the selection) to move it, drag from an output dot to an input to
wire them, and press a wire's × to remove it. The minimap pans where you press. Every
move, wire and removal is announced, and each node's description says what it's wired to
("Inputs: Prompt from Answer template Prompt.").

## For agents

`addNode(kind, title?, x?, y?)`, `moveNode(node, x, y)`, `connect(from, to, fromPort?,
toPort?)`, `disconnect(from, to)`, `select(...nodes)`, `openNode(node)` and `fitView()`,
by titles (or ids, when two share a title). A wire that isn't allowed, an unknown kind or
port, or a locked node says why. `query({ within: "Workflow" })` lists each node as
`{ value: id, label: "Draft answer (at 600, 130; Inputs: …; Outputs: …)" }`. Removing goes
through the toolbar's Remove button, marked `data-agent-confirm`, so a person approves it.

## Known limits

Find in page doesn't reveal nodes off screen yet (UI SDK's `bindFindable` can add it).
Very large graphs (thousands of nodes) render every node; virtualizing them is future
work.


<!-- docs/ide.md -->

# IDE

The parts of a code editor, on UI SDK's Tree, Tabs, Command, Dialog and Textarea, plus an
**IDE page** template that puts them together in resizable panes.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @uiset/ide       # the parts
npx shadcn@latest add @uiset/ide-app   # the whole page
```

## Parts

| Part             | What it is                                                                                         |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `FileTree`       | Files on UI SDK's Tree, folders first, version control marks; New file, New folder, Rename, Move, Delete |
| `EditorTabs`     | Open files on UI SDK's Tabs: unsaved dots, same-named files told apart by folder, closing             |
| `CodeEditor`     | A textarea with line numbers, syntax colors (shiki, themed by every skin), indenting and problems    |
| `CommandPalette` | Go to a file (⌘P), run a command (⌘⇧P, or start with `>`), go to a line (start with `:`)              |
| `ProblemsList`   | Problems worst first; choosing one opens its file at the line                                         |
| `StatusBar`      | The bottom strip: `StatusBarItem`s as text or buttons                                                 |
| `IdeTemplate`    | All of it, with a sample project, a tiny linter, an outline, save and unsaved-close prompts           |

## Use

```tsx
<FileTree label="Files" paths={paths} value={selected} onValueChange={setSelected}
  onOpen={openFile} status={{ "src/app.ts": "modified" }}
  onCreate={create} onRename={rename} onMove={move} onDelete={remove} />

<EditorTabs files={open.map((path) => ({ path, dirty: isDirty(path) }))} value={active}
  onValueChange={setActive}
  onClose={(path) => (isDirty(path) ? askFirst(path) : closeTab(path, nextTab(open, path)))}>
  {(path) => (
    <CodeEditor ref={(handle) => editors.set(path, handle)} label={path} path={path} value={files[path]}
      onValueChange={(text) => write(path, text)} onCursorChange={setCursor}
      problems={problems.filter((p) => p.path === path)} />
  )}
</EditorTabs>

<CommandPalette files={paths} recent={recent} commands={commands}
  onOpenFile={openFile} onCommand={run} onGoToLine={(line) => editor.current?.goTo(line)} />
```

- `paths` lists files; a path ending in `/` is an empty folder. Folders come from the paths.
- `onCreate`, `onRename` and `onMove` get the full new path (or the target folder) and may
  return a message to refuse; the dialog shows it. Names that exist or hold a slash are
  refused before your handler runs. Deleting asks first (`data-agent-confirm`).
- `status` marks files `modified`, `added`, `deleted`, `untracked` or `conflict`: a letter
  and a color on screen, the word in the item's name. Folders say "has changes".
- `EditorTabs` asks to close through `onClose`; the file closes when you drop it from
  `files` and pick the next `value` (`nextTab(paths, path)` gives the neighbor). So `onClose`
  can ask about unsaved changes first. Once it's gone, focus goes to the tab that took
  over, or to the empty pane. Every open file keeps its own panel, so each editor keeps its
  caret, scroll and undo while another tab shows.
- `CodeEditor` takes `path` or `language` for colors, `readOnly`, `tabSize` and `problems`.
  Its handle has `focus()` and `goTo(line, col)`. It keeps its own undo (UI SDK's
  `createUndoStack`): a run of typing is one step until a pause or a caret move, and Tab,
  Enter and outside changes are steps of their own. In Chrome any text change on the page
  while typing ends the browser's own undo step, so a colored editor can't rely on it.
- The text stays the textarea's own while you type and reaches `onValueChange` once a
  frame; text you change from outside is written back. Lines keep their colors while an
  edit is being colored. The colors come from `--shiki-*` variables in `code/code.css`,
  checked at 4.5:1 in every skin, and still 4.5:1 under the selection (`--code-selection`).
- The editor is a plain textarea underneath, so screen readers, spell check (off by
  default), autofill and agents all treat it as text.

## Keys

| Where       | Keys                         | Does                                                     |
| ----------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Anywhere    | ⌘P / Ctrl+P                  | Go to a file                                             |
| Anywhere    | ⌘⇧P / Ctrl+Shift+P           | Run a command; `:` then a number goes to a line          |
| File tree   | Arrows, Home, End, Enter     | UI SDK's Tree; Enter opens a file                        |
| File tree   | F2, Delete                   | Rename, delete (asks first)                              |
| Tabs        | Arrows, Delete               | UI SDK's Tabs; Delete closes the focused tab             |
| Editor      | Tab, Shift+Tab               | Indent, outdent (every selected line)                    |
| Editor      | Enter                        | New line, keeping the indent; one deeper after `{`       |
| Editor      | Escape, then Tab             | Leave the editor (Tab moves focus on like anywhere else) |
| Editor      | F8, Shift+F8                 | Next and previous problem, read out                      |
| Editor      | Page Up, Page Down           | The caret by a screenful (Shift selects)                 |
| Editor      | ⌘Z, ⌘⇧Z (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y)     | Undo and redo, a run of typing at a time                 |
| IDE page    | ⌘S / Ctrl+S                  | Save                                                     |

## For agents

Every part is a UI SDK component, so agents use it by name: choosing a file in **Files**
(`setValue`) opens it, as Enter does for a person; switch tabs, write code in the editor
named by its path (`setValue`), press New file and fill the dialog, or choose a problem.
Deleting goes through the confirm. UI SDK's Command doesn't yet let agents run a
command (reported upstream), so palette commands are people-only for now.

## Known limits

The editor draws every line, so it suits files up to about a thousand lines; it isn't a
full code editor engine (no virtualized lines, multiple cursors, folding or completion).
The template keeps files in memory: pass `onSave` to write them, and `lint` for your own
linter or language server's problems.


<!-- docs/mobile.md -->

# Mobile

The parts of a phone app, on UI SDK's gesture behaviors and components. Every gesture has
a keyboard path and a screen reader path, and every part works with a mouse too.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @uiset/mobile
```

## Parts

| Part                 | What it is                                                                                   |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SwipeList`          | Rows that swipe aside to actions on either side; a long swipe runs the first (`createSwipeActions`) |
| `PullToRefresh`      | Pull down at the top to refresh, with resistance (`rubberBand`); a Refresh button for the keyboard |
| `WheelPicker`        | A wheel you scroll to choose from (`bindScrollPicker` on a Listbox)                          |
| `TimeWheel`          | Hour, minute and AM/PM wheels, as `"HH:MM"`                                                  |
| `Sheet`              | A bottom sheet, as tall as its content or resting at snap points (Drawer)                     |
| `ActionSheet`        | A sheet of choices with Cancel; `await sheet.choose()` returns the one chosen                |
| `AppBar`, `TabBar`   | The top bar (back, title, actions) and the bottom bar (sections, the current one marked)     |

## Use

```tsx
function Inbox() {
  const [sheet] = useState(createActionSheet)
  const options = async () => {
    const choice = await sheet.choose() // "read-all", or undefined for Cancel
    if (choice === "read-all") markAllRead()
  }
  return (
    <>
      <AppBar title="Inbox" actions={<Button aria-label="Inbox options" onClick={() => void options()}>…</Button>} />
      <PullToRefresh onRefresh={() => fetchMail()} onError={report}>
        <SwipeList
          label="Messages"
          items={messages.map((m) => ({
            id: m.id,
            label: `${m.from}: ${m.subject}`,
            content: <MessageRow message={m} />,
            start: [{ id: "read", label: "Read", icon: "mail" }],
            end: [
              { id: "archive", label: "Archive", icon: "archive", tone: "neutral" },
              { id: "delete", label: "Delete", icon: "trash", tone: "danger" },
            ],
          }))}
          onOpen={open}
          onAction={(id, action) => run(id, action)}
        />
      </PullToRefresh>
      <ActionSheet controller={sheet} title="Inbox" actions={[{ value: "read-all", label: "Mark all as read" }]} />
      <TabBar value={tab} onValueChange={setTab}
        items={[{ id: "inbox", label: "Inbox", icon: "inbox", badge: 2 }, { id: "alarms", label: "Alarms", icon: "bell" }]} />
    </>
  )
}

<Sheet title="New alarm" open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <TimeWheel label="Alarm time" value={time} onValueChange={setTime} />
</Sheet>

<Sheet title="Help" snapPoints={[0.5, 1]} trigger={<DrawerTrigger>Help</DrawerTrigger>}>…</Sheet>
```

- `start` actions show by swiping toward the end (left to right in English), `end` actions
  the other way; it flips in right-to-left pages. A side's first action sits at the row's
  edge. Past `fullSwipe` (0.6 of the row) that action fills the row, and letting go runs it
  and announces it. Hidden actions are inert.
- After an action, focus goes back to its row, or, if the row went (archived, deleted), to
  the row now in its place. A tap on an open row closes it instead of opening the row.
- Each row with actions also has an Actions menu. It's out of the tab order (a row is one tab
  stop) and out of sight, but screen readers reach it with their own keys and swipes, where
  neither swipes nor arrows reach the actions; it shows while it has focus.
- A row without `label` is named by its content's text.
- `PullToRefresh` waits for its `onRefresh` Promise. A rejected one is announced ("Couldn't
  refresh.") and handed to `onError`. Pulls only start at the top and only downward, so the
  list still scrolls; a short pull springs back. The pull moves by a CSS variable, so a pull
  doesn't re-render the list.
- A `Sheet` with one snap point (the default, `"content"`) is as tall as its content and has
  a plain bar. With more it's 85% of the screen, UI SDK's limit for a drawer, and its handle
  is a button that steps through the points. Drawer's other props (`dismissible`,
  `defaultOpen`, `modalAbove`, …) pass through.
- `WheelPicker` keeps focus on its value: when the value changes from outside, focus in the
  wheel moves with it, so nothing that reveals the focused option scrolls the wheel back.
  `TimeWheel` shows a value between its `minuteStep`s too (07 with a step of 5).
- A `TabBar` item with `href` is a link, and a click with a modifier key is left to the
  browser (a new tab); without `href` it's a UI SDK Button. Badges are a number on screen and
  words in the name ("Inbox, 2 new").
- `AppBar` takes `headingLevel` (1 by default) to fit the page's outline.
- Accent text uses `--mobile-accent`, the primary pulled toward the text color so it clears
  4.5:1 in every skin. Focus on a filled swipe action is drawn in its own text color.

## Keys

| Part          | Keys                                                                 |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SwipeList     | Up and Down between rows (one tab stop); Left and Right show a row's actions and focus the first; Escape closes them; Enter opens the row |
| PullToRefresh | Tab reaches a Refresh button at the top of the list                  |
| WheelPicker   | Arrows, Home, End, Page Up and Down, and typing, like any Listbox     |
| Sheet         | Escape closes; the handle steps through snap points with Enter, or arrows, Home and End |

## Touch

Rows swipe with a finger without stopping the list from scrolling up and down
(`touch-action: pan-y`). At the top of the list, a finger pulling down is the refresh's,
and scrolling down stays the browser's. Nothing gets selected while a row swipes or the
list pulls. Wheels snap to an option (`scroll-snap-type`).

## For agents

- **Messages** (the `SwipeList`'s label): `runAction(row, action)` runs a row's action by
  names people see, like `runAction("Ada Lovelace", "Archive")`; `openRow(row)` opens one. Agents read the
  rows with `query`, each with its actions. A `danger` action isn't run this way: the step
  fails with "Needs a person" and points at the row's Actions menu, whose item carries
  `data-agent-confirm`, so pressing it there asks the person.
- `ActionSheet` choices marked `destructive` carry `data-agent-confirm` too.
- Tab bar sections, app bar buttons, wheels (`setValue` on "Alarm time, hour") and sheets are
  UI SDK components agents use by name.

## Other languages

Every word the parts say is a prop: `SwipeList messages` (`help`, `actionsFor`),
`PullToRefresh messages` (`refresh`, `pull`, `release`, `refreshing`, `done`, `failed`),
`TimeWheel labels` (`hour`, `minute`, `period`, `am`, `pm`), `Sheet resizeLabel`,
`ActionSheet cancelLabel`, `TabBar label` and `badgeLabel`, `AppBar backLabel`.

## Known limits

- With reduced motion, a press on a sheet's handle in the first moments after it opens
  closes it instead of resizing it (UI SDK's Drawer; reported upstream).
- `TimeWheel` is a 12- or 24-hour clock in its own words; it doesn't read the page's locale.


<!-- docs/terminal.md -->

# Terminal

A terminal for commands your app defines, like a web shell, a dev console or a CLI in the
browser. Built on UI SDK's `createInputHistory` (Up and Down) and a `ScrollArea` with
`stickToEnd` (output follows its end unless you scroll up).

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @uiset/terminal
```

## Use

```tsx
<Terminal
  label="Shell"
  prompt="~/app $"
  welcome="Type help for the commands."
  commands={{
    echo: { description: "Prints its words", usage: "<words…>", run: (args) => args.join(" ") },
    cat: {
      description: "Prints a file",
      usage: "<file>",
      complete: () => Object.keys(files),
      run: (args, io) => io.print(read(args[0])),
    },
    build: {
      description: "Builds, with a progress bar",
      async *run(_args, io) {
        for (let p = 0; p <= 100; p += 10) {
          await step(io.signal)
          yield `\r${p}%`
        }
        yield "\n\x1b[32m✓\x1b[0m done\n"
      },
    },
  }}
  onCommand={(line, io) => sendToServer(line, { signal: io.signal, onOutput: io.print })}
/>

// Output from elsewhere, like a socket:
const [shell] = useState(createTerminalController)
<Terminal label="Shell" controller={shell} … />
socket.onmessage = (event) => shell.print(event.data)
```

- A command's `run(args, io)` returns a string, a Promise of one, nothing (after calling
  `io.print` and `io.error`), or an async iterable that streams. A thrown error prints in the
  danger tone. `io.signal` aborts on Ctrl+C, and the prompt comes back at once even if the
  command doesn't listen.
- Output goes through a small screen with a cursor, as a real terminal's does: `\r` returns to
  the line's start and what follows overwrites it (progress bars), `\b` steps back, and the
  erase-line, column and cursor-up codes spinners use (`\e[2K`, `\e[G`, `\e[A`) redraw in
  place. An escape split across two chunks waits for the rest; styles carry across lines.
- ANSI styles: the 16 colors as 9 tokens (bright black is a muted grey), backgrounds as tints,
  bold, dim, italic, underline, strikethrough, and inverse as a solid fill (so test runners'
  PASS and FAIL badges stay readable). 256-color and true-color codes keep the skin's colors.
  URLs and OSC 8 links become links, http(s) only. Control and bidi-override characters are
  dropped.
- The page catches up once a frame, however fast output comes, and only changed lines draw
  again. Past `scrollback` lines (2000), old lines go even while you're scrolled up, and
  what you're reading stays put.
- `help`, `clear` and `history` come built in. `onCommand` gets lines no command matched.
- `messages` replaces the terminal's own words, for other languages.
- `controller` (`createTerminalController()`) writes output (`print`, `error`), runs and clears
  from outside, like a socket's messages.
- `scrollback` caps the lines kept (2000).
- The colors are `--term-red` and friends, checked at 4.5:1 on the terminal in every skin and
  scheme. "Black" and "white" follow the scheme instead of vanishing into it.

## Keys

| Keys              | Does                                                                 |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter             | Runs the line                                                        |
| Up, Down          | Earlier and later commands; Down past the newest brings back your draft |
| Tab               | Completes a command, or an argument with `complete` (quoting words with spaces); a second Tab lists several. With nothing to complete, Tab moves on |
| Ctrl+C            | Stops the running command, or drops the line; with text selected, copies |
| Ctrl+L            | Clears the screen                                                    |
